newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric urges shareholders to reject bid.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric urges shareholders to reject bid.

text.p: British regional electricity distributor Northern Electric on Tuesday urged its shareholders to reject a hostile bid by CE Electric.
CE Electric, which launched the 650 million pound ($1.07 billion) takeover attempt last week, is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the U.S.
Earlier it posted its offer document for Northern Electric and said that since its offer was announced shareholders had sold it around 13.4 percent of the ordinary shares.

Northern Electric rejected last week's bid, the second unwanted advance it has faced in two years and the fourth U.S. offer for one of Britain's cash-rich regional electricity companies in a wave of takeovers in the sector.

Northern Electric's chairman David Morris said the offer would deprive shareholders of a special dividend as well as the interim dividend. It "substantially undervalues Northern Electric. It should be rejected," he said.
Morris said Northern Electric would show that it had created value since it was last subject to a hostile takeover.

Trafalgar House was the first predator attracted by the huge cashflow Britain's electricity suppliers had amassed since privatisation in 1990 and launched a hostile bid for Northern Electric in December 1994.
A surprise decision by the industry regulator three months later to reopen his price review of the electricity sector sent power shares crashing.

With regulatory uncertainty shrouding the future profitability of electricity companies, Trafalgar House allowed its original bid to lapse and was itself subsequently taken over by the Kvaerner engineering group of Norway. ($1=.6051 Pound)
